chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: 'I'm Coming Virginia', an unusual song she still sings
summary: She discusses the song's unusual 24-bar structure, its early recordings and keeping it in her repertoire forty years on.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: "I'm Coming Virginia."
Yes.
Which got me thinking when I was looking over this discography, it's an unusual song. And it's not the normal 32-bar chorus, but the construction is 24 bars, I think.
Yeah.
With three sections and --
Well "I'm Coming Virginia" was one of my own songs. That is, it's more of a thing that I had been doing, you know, previous to that.
"I'm Coming Virginia" has always been a favorite of mine. It's always been a good instrumental.

I think one of the first recordings I heard of it -- and this was even before I came to New York or thought I ever was going to do anything in show business, that Tea garden -- it's not a new -- it wasn't a new song.
Looking at my notes, I see it was written in 1927.
